candidate.answerReason: Tangency determines the large circle's radius as 3. Subtracting the areas of the seven unit circles from its area gives 9π−7π=2π.

methods.label: Find the enclosing radius and subtract
methods.explanation:
The shaded region is everything inside the large circle except the seven small disks. Thus we need the large radius before subtracting their areas.

Let \(O\) be the innermost circle's center. Two externally tangent circles of radius \(1\) have centers \(2\) units apart. Therefore each surrounding center is \(2\) units from \(O\), and neighboring surrounding centers are also \(2\) units apart. Joining \(O\) to two neighboring centers forms an equilateral triangle, so consecutive surrounding centers are spaced by \(60^\circ\) around \(O\).

We must also justify that the large circle has center \(O\). Let its center be \(C\) and its radius be \(r\). Internal tangency to each surrounding unit circle gives a center distance of \(r-1\). Thus \(C\) is equally distant from all six surrounding centers. The point \(O\) is also equally distant from them. Three of those centers are noncollinear, and their perpendicular bisectors have a unique intersection, so \(C=O\).

The distance from the large center to any surrounding center is consequently \(2\). Adding the small radius gives
\[
r=2+1=3.
\]
The seven small disks have disjoint interiors, so their areas can be subtracted once each:
\[
A_{\text{shaded}}=\pi(3)^2-7\pi(1)^2
=9\pi-7\pi=\boxed{2\pi}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).

review.mathematicalCheck: Tangency places all surrounding centers 2 units from the innermost center. Internal tangency makes the enclosing center equidistant from those centers. Uniqueness of the perpendicular-bisector intersection for three noncollinear centers proves concentricity, hence enclosing radius 3. The shading shown is precisely the enclosing disk minus the seven unit disks, giving 9π-7π = 2π.
